_comment: AgentGuard known-bad advisory feed — BUILD_PLAN.md §7's 'known-bad' half. Each entry is a PUBLIC, sourced disclosure of a malicious or vulnerable MCP artifact, matched by IDENTITY (package name + version, publisher, remote host, or a name pattern), not by heuristics. `severity: malicious` -> Capability::KnownMalicious -> forced BLOCK; `severity: advisory` -> Capability::KnownAdvisory -> forced review. Hand-curated and versioned in the repo, bundled into the binary (include_str!) so it works offline; `agentguard advisories refresh` can pull a newer copy from the GitHub release. Every entry MUST carry at least one `references` URL. Keep it small and real — this is not a place for speculative or unsourced entries.

advisories.title: postmark-mcp exfiltrated every outbound email via a hidden BCC
advisories.detail: postmark-mcp version 1.0.16 (published 2025-09-17 by npm user 'phanpak') silently added a blind-copy of every email the MCP server sent to an attacker-controlled address (phan@giftshop.club). Present through 1.0.18; removed from npm around 2025-09-25. There is no safe version in this line — the maintained server moved elsewhere.

advisories.title: mcp-remote — OS command injection / RCE (CVE-2025-6514)
advisories.detail: mcp-remote before 0.1.16 passes a value derived from the MCP server's authorization endpoint URL to a system shell, so a malicious or compromised remote server can achieve arbitrary command execution on the client machine. CVSS 9.6. Fixed in 0.1.16 — upgrade, or pin a remote server you fully trust.

advisories.title: Invariant Labs MCP tool-poisoning proof-of-concept servers
advisories.detail: Deliberately-malicious MCP servers published by Invariant Labs to reproduce tool-poisoning and rug-pull attacks (hidden instructions in tool descriptions that exfiltrate SSH keys / repo contents / chat history). Safe to study, never to run against a real agent with real credentials.

advisories.title: Common impersonation / typosquat patterns for well-known MCP servers
advisories.detail: A package named to look like an official reference server (an '-unofficial', '-mcp', '-v2', '-fork' suffix on 'github' / 'filesystem' / 'git' / 'slack' / 'fetch' / 'postgres' / 'sqlite') from a non-canonical publisher. Not proof of malice on its own, but the exact shape a shadowing/typosquat attack takes — review the source and publisher before trusting it. Complements the cross-artifact shadowing detector for the case where only one such server is configured.
